contexts.text: As (seven = what is sacred) both the greater and the lesser intervals of time were distinguished into sevens, and were called weeks. Illustrated. AC 728:2. AC 728:4.
The time of seven days, or of one week, = the beginning of temptation; and fourteen, or that of two weeks, = the same.
The last time of the Church is signified by the third day, the third week, etc.

A week, which is seven days, = an entire period of any state or time, as of reformation, of regeneration, of temptation, both of a man in particular, and of the Church in general. Thus a period, whether of a thousand years, of a hundred, of ten, or of as many days, hours, or minutes, is called a week. And as the eighth day is the first day of the following week, it = any beginning. AC 2213:end.

Fulfil this week () = a further succession of the study or earnest diligence; (for) a week = a state, and also an entire period; here, therefore, the sequent state and period, consequently, what is successive... When a week is mentioned in the singular, it = the end of a prior state and the beginning of the sequent one, thus a new state, to fulfil which, is [to do so] from beginning to end. The reason a week = like all times in special = is a state, also a period, is that all states have their periods, that is, their beginning, succession, and end; yet, in the other life, these are not perceived as times, but as states and their successive developments. In this instance it is evident that... by a week the ancients understood any period that was distinguished into seven parts, whether it was one of days, years, or ages... for it here means a period of seven years. And as, with them, seven = what is holy, a week = a holy period, and also what is holy of a period.

For weeks, in the Word, = an entire period, great or small; and when two weeks are mentioned together (as a fortnight, or fourteen years) the signification is the same; because the doubling... of a number does not take away its signification.
Seven days were fulfilled () = the end of that state... For seven days = an entire period from beginning to end, thus a full state, like a week. 7890. AC 8421.
Seven weeks even to Messiah the Prince () = that the Lord will come in the fulness of time; thus an entire period is signified.
A week = what is full.
Forty-two months = the same as six weeks; and six weeks = the same as the six days of one week... and a week = an entire period, greater or smaller.
Let people resist evils in intention even once a week, or twice in a month, and they will perceive a change.
Hence it is that a week, in Daniel and elsewhere = an entire period from beginning to end, and is predicated of the Church.

Six weeks = what is complete even to the end; for six has this signification; and a week = a state; and seven weeks, a holy state, which is the state of a new Church, when the Lord commences His Kingdom.
Seven = the beginning and the end, thus an entire period, and a full state, like a week.

Forty-two = the end of the former Church and the beginning of the new one... because this number means six weeks, which = the same as the six days of one week, namely, a state of combat and labour, and thus the end when the Church has been completely vastated, or when evil has been consummated; and the seventh week, which then follows, = the beginning of the new Church... Six weeks also = what is plenary and complete.
In the Word, all times, as weeks, = states. AE 673.
Seventy weeks are decreed upon thy people () = the time and state of the Church which then existed among the Jews.
Seven weeks () = a full time and state.
After sixty-two weeks it shall be restored... () = the full time and state after His coming... AE 684:38.

He shall confirm a covenant for one week () = the time of the Reformation, when the Word was again read and the Lord acknowledged, that is, the Divine in His Human... The time of the Reformation is signified by one week.

But in the midst of the week, be shall cause the sacrifice and meat-offering to cease () = that still interiorly with those who were reformed there would be no truth and good in the worship... The midst of the week does not signify the middle of that time, but the inmost of the state with the Reformed... a week = the state of the Church.
